description: Patch releases of Autobrr are NOT automerged here, and the reason is that Autobrr migrates its own database on every start. The container's first log lines are `preparing to apply base schema migration` on a fresh install and `database schema up to date` afterwards; v1.84.0 ships 95 numbered migrations under internal/database/migrations, and they are forward-only - there is no down step and no flag an operator could withhold. A bumped image therefore rewrites the schema holding the operator's filters, indexer and download-client credentials and release history, unattended, on the next restart.

The measurement, so that this can be revisited rather than re-argued: across the 20 patch spans this project has published (v1.24.1, v1.26.1, v1.26.2, v1.27.1, v1.34.1, v1.35.1, v1.38.1, v1.39.1, v1.40.1, v1.46.1, v1.47.1, v1.51.1, v1.53.1, v1.56.1, v1.63.1, v1.66.1, v1.72.1, v1.75.1, v1.77.1, v1.82.1), 17 did not touch migration code at all, 1 added a new migration outright (v1.38.0..v1.38.1, an UPDATE of irc_network), and 2 edited the SQL of migrations that already existed (v1.56.1, v1.63.1). Not zero, and the two in-place edits are the kind of change that a `did the migration count go up` test would miss.

There is also very little to buy. Autobrr publishes patch releases rarely - v1.75.1, v1.77.1 and v1.82.1 are the only ones in the whole v1.7x-v1.8x range - so nearly every update Renovate opens here is a minor, which this preset leaves for review regardless. A rare automerge against a forward-only schema migration is the wrong side of that trade. Minor and patch bumps alike stay human-reviewed pull requests; the Molecule run still gates them.

What that Molecule run does gate is real, and is worth knowing when this is reconsidered. It stands up the role, then runs the same image with none of the role's configuration to establish what an unconfigured Autobrr picks for itself - it starts, migrates and serves the same web UI, so the scenario rests only on values Autobrr does not choose: the port, the log level, the update-check setting and the timezone the role rendered into its env file. It gates on the readiness endpoint rather than on the unit being `active`, checks that anonymous calls get 403 and forged API tokens 401, walks onboarding from 204 to 503, asserts /api/config reports the version `autobrr_version` pins alongside the image tag and the image's OCI version label, round-trips a filter through the API and finds the row in the SQLite file on the host path the role mounts, and watches NRestarts across a window longer than RestartSec. A patch bump that broke startup, the schema or the API would fail there. What it cannot see is the silent, successful migration of an existing operator's database, which is the risk this decision is about.

`versioning=semver` on the annotation in defaults/main.yml is load-bearing and must stay. Of the 1430 tags ghcr.io/autobrr/autobrr carries, 1234 are per-pull-request `pr-NNNN` tags and another 63 are `latest`, `develop`, `master`, release candidates, and floating minors from `v1.35` through `v1.84`. Strict semver leaves exactly the 133 real vX.Y.Z releases; without it the floating `v1.84` would be a candidate, which is how a role in this fleet once ended up following a floating major.
